source_ref: Pellerin N, Raufaste E (2020) 'Psychological Resources Protect Well-Being During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Longitudinal Study During the French Lockdown', Frontiers in Psychology 11:590276, doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2020.590276 (CC BY 4.0; PMC7793808). DATA: OSF project https://osf.io/45aq3/, file data.PsyR_lockdown2020.csv (https://osf.io/download/dc6me/, sha256 4909d4819b8b6682eaf7db347e702afd20088b979f43cd09667160cd8b7db5fb). Processing script: data/pellerin2020_covid_resources.py. ITEM TEXT: Koller I, Levenson MR, Glueck J (2017) 'What Do You Think You Are Measuring? A Mixed-Methods Procedure for Assessing the Content Validity of Test Items and Theory-Based Scaling', Frontiers in Psychology 8:126, doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2017.00126 (CC BY 4.0; PMC5318383), Table 3B, which prints the seven self-transcendence items against their ASTI item numbers; cross-checked verbatim against MPsychoR 0.10-8's ASTI help page, https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/MPsychoR/html/ASTI.html. Original instrument: Levenson MR, Jennings PA, Aldwin CM, Shiraishi RW (2005) 'Self-transcendence: conceptualization and measurement', Int J Aging Hum Dev 60:127-143. RESPONSE ANCHORS: Pellerin & Raufaste Materials section. MAPPING CHECK: the ASTI reference dataset in MPsychoR (data('ASTI'), n=1,215; 1,129 complete on the ST block), whose ST inter-item correlations reproduce the matrix in Koller et al.'s Appendix (DataSheet1.docx, Europe PMC supplementaryFiles for PMC5318383). Sources cached under itemtext/.cache/pellerin2020_asti/.
note: PASS with disclosures. 49 rows = 7 items x 7 response levels; validate_items.R --table-sets passes on both sets (ST_1..ST_7; resp 1-7). irw_table_sets reports 7,070 live rows, n=1,010 per item, resp range 1-7 for every item; irw_fetch() was never called. (1) INSTRUMENT (Step 3b): confirmed the ASTI, self-transcendence dimension. data/pellerin2020_covid_resources.py melts exactly [f'ST_{i}' for i in range(1,8)] out of the OSF file; Pellerin & Raufaste's Materials section states they used 'the most recently published version of the Adult Self-Transcendence Inventory (ASTI, Koller et al., 2017)' and 'selected all seven items of the dimension of self-transcendence ... (e.g., "I feel that my individual life is part of a greater whole", alpha = 0.81)' -- that example is ASTI item 2 verbatim; and re-running the authors' own reliability line alpha(dat0[grep('ST_',...)]) under their exact exclusions (non-France, single-response, minor, gender='other'; n=470 at wave 0) returns alpha = 0.81, the figure the paper prints. Koller et al.'s ST dimension has exactly 7 items. No mismatch. (2) SHIPPED WORDING IS ENGLISH; THE STUDY ADMINISTERED FRENCH. The OSF deposit (osf.io/45aq3) holds exactly two files -- PsyR_lockdown2020.R and data.PsyR_lockdown2020.csv, confirmed against the OSF v2 file listing on 2026-09-20. The CSV is a bare header row (ST_1..ST_7, zero non-ASCII characters anywhere in it) with no variable or value labels; the .R is an lme4/mediation analysis script with no item strings. The Frontiers article has no supplementary material (the string 'supplementary' does not occur anywhere in the article HTML). Per the 2026-09-01 fallback rule the ASTI's published English goes in the base fields, the _translated columns are omitted, language=French, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english. No machine translation was produced. (3) TEXT IS VERBATIM AND DOUBLE-SOURCED. Item wording transcribed character-for-character from Koller, Levenson & Glueck (2017) Front Psychol 8:126 (CC BY 4.0), Table 3B, and independently confirmed against MPsychoR's ASTI help page (?MPsychoR::ASTI), which prints all 25 item wordings with their dimension tags; the two agree exactly, including the published bracket notation in 'Whatever [good] I do for others, I do for myself.' and 'Whatever [bad] I do to others, I do to myself.' The brackets are the source's own and were NOT edited out. (4) OPTION TEXT. Only the two anchors the paper publishes are shipped ('strongly disagree'=1, 'strongly agree'=7); scale points 2-6 are unlabelled in the source and were left blank, not padded with their own numbers. Note the ASTI is normally administered on its own 3-4 point 'compared to five years ago' format; this study re-scaled it to the uniform 1-7 agreement scale it used for every resource, which is what the live resp range shows. (5) MAPPING IS ORDER-INFERRED AND ONLY PARTLY VERIFIED (Step 5b, PARTIAL). The IRW item code IS the source column name (code-derivation pattern 1), but that CSV ties the code to nothing textual, so ST_k -> the k-th ASTI self-transcendence item (ASTI2, ASTI4, ASTI7, ASTI13, ASTI16, ASTI24, ASTI25) is a presentation-order inference. Checked against the data: scoring all 5040 permutations of the 7x7 inter-item correlation matrix against the same seven items' matrix in the MPsychoR ASTI reference sample (n=1,129, the data behind Koller et al.'s Appendix) puts the shipped mapping FIRST by both Pearson (r=0.8987) and Spearman (rho=0.8519). It pins ST_4=ASTI13 and ST_6/ST_7=ASTI24/ASTI25 decisively, but the runner-up permutations -- ST_1<->ST_3 and ST_2<->ST_5 -- are within 0.009 of it, so ASTI2 vs ASTI7 and ASTI4 vs ASTI16 are NOT separated by the data. See verify_pellerin2020_asti.R. (6) RIGHTS: no reserved-right clause locatable or quotable for the ASTI. The seven items are printed in full in a CC BY 4.0 Frontiers article by the instrument's own co-author (Levenson) and redistributed in CRAN's MPsychoR (GPL-3) help page; a targeted search for an ASTI permission/copyright/licence statement returned no rights-holder page stating a fee, a permission requirement, a non-commercial term, a no-derivatives term or a redistribution bar. Silence is permission, so not blocked; no register row written (a round may not write a 'ship' row).
public_note: Item text for pellerin2020_asti is the ASTI's published English wording; the study administered the scale in French and no French version of the items or of the 1-7 anchors appears in its OSF deposit or its article, so what is shown here is a parallel English version rather than the sentences respondents actually read. The item-to-code mapping is a presentation-order inference that the response data confirms only in part: it ranks first of all 5040 possible assignments, and it fixes ST_4, ST_6 and ST_7, but it cannot distinguish ST_1 from ST_3 ('I feel that my individual life is a part of a greater whole' vs 'I feel part of something greater than myself', which correlate 0.76) or ST_2 from ST_5 ('...belonging with both earlier and future generations' vs '...oneness with nature'), so either of those two pairs could be swapped.

Confirmed arithmetically: the deposit's own 职业期望 column is EXACTLY the raw mean of B1..B21 (max |diff| 5.3e-15 over 506 complete rows), and its three subscale columns 职业声望 / 自我发展 / 福利收入 are exact raw means of a unique 8/8/5 partition of the same block. This is the same dictionary/name fix already owed from batches 229 and 230 for four of this deposit's six tables (irw#2198); it is a response-data/dictionary fix, not an item-text fix. (2) TEXT: item_text is the administered Chinese transcribed verbatim from Data_Sheet_2.PDF section 二 (题号 1-21, 项目 column); item_text_translated, instructions_translated and option_text_translated are IRW's own English (machine_translation) -- no published English rendering of this scale exists, so an issues-page entry is owed. (3) OPTIONS: the administered anchors are the printed importance grid 不太重要 / 一般 / 有些重要 / 重要 / 很重要 = 1..5. NOTE the paper's Measures section instead describes the scale as "a five-point Likert scale ranging from 1 (completely disagree) to 5 (completely agree)"; the questionnaire the respondents actually filled in prints the importance anchors, and those are what is shipped. No reverse-keyed items: all 21 are positively worded attributes and the study's own aggregates are raw means, so the stored direction is as printed. (4) MAPPING VERIFICATION IS PARTIAL -- the recovered 8/8/5 partition agrees with the content of the shipped wording at all 21 positions, but it does not order items within a subscale; see verification_wu2021_empathy.csv. Mechanism unknown; irw#2195. The item text shipped here is unaffected by it, but an analyst using this table should know. (6) RIGHTS: no quotable restriction located for the Occupation Expectation Scale. The originator is a 2001 应用心理学 article with no distribution page of its own; searches for a rights-holder page carrying stated terms (the shape found for the LBUS and CD-RISC siblings in this same deposit) returned none, and the wording IRW copies is the study's own Chinese administration published in a CC BY 4.0 Frontiers supplement.
